 Liverpool have made contact over move to sign Tottenham Hotspur star 
 Go to the comments section Add to your bookmarks Share this article Pedro Porro Transfer Latest as Liverpool Assess Right-Back Options
 Liverpool’s long-term planning at right-back is coming into sharper focus, and Pedro Porro has now entered the conversation. According to TeamTalk , the Tottenham defender is among the names being considered as Liverpool weigh up how to strengthen that area in 2027.
 The situation is layered. Conor Bradley remains highly regarded internally, but a lengthy absence has inevitably created uncertainty around how quickly he can return to his best level. Liverpool are understood to retain faith in the Northern Ireland international, though a full assessment will only come once he is back playing regularly and consistently.
 OneFootball Videos
 There is further intrigue around Jeremie Frimpong. Reports suggest he could look to move on after failing to fully establish himself following his 2025 arrival. If that position does open up, Liverpool may have little choice but to enter the market for proven quality.
 Pedro Porro emerges in Liverpool transfer thinking
 Porro fits the broad profile. He is experienced, attack-minded and tested in the Premier League. TeamTalk report that Liverpool have made enquiries over his availability, with Tottenham prepared to listen for the right fee. From a recruitment standpoint, that makes him a logical option to monitor.
 There is, however, an important complication. The same report states that Porro would favour a return to Spain over a move elsewhere in England. Liverpool, Manchester City and Chelsea are all mentioned as interested parties, but Barcelona and Real Madrid are believed to hold stronger appeal for the 27-year-old if either club turn that admiration into something more concrete.
 Photo: IMAGO
 Right-back market may hinge on Spain decision
 That leaves Liverpool in a familiar waiting game. Porro’s preference appears clear, and unless the Spanish giants step back, any Premier League suitor may struggle to shift the direction of travel. Even so, Liverpool are right to keep him under consideration. Players with his blend of creativity, energy and top-level experience do not often become realistically available.
 Much will still depend on Bradley’s recovery and on whether Frimpong’s future changes. Liverpool’s recruitment team are unlikely to rush, but the right-back position increasingly looks like one to watch closely over the next 12 months.
 Our View
 If Liverpool are seriously looking ahead at right-back, that feels sensible. Too much has been left hanging in that area and it is far better to act early than wait for another season to drift into uncertainty. Bradley has talent and character, but a year out is significant for any young player, especially in a role that demands rhythm, confidence and repeated high-level sprints.
 Porro would be an exciting option. He has the aggression, technical quality and attacking thrust to suit a big club, and he would immediately raise the level of competition. Even if his heart is set on Spain, Liverpool should still be in these conversations. Clubs with serious ambitions need to test the market for top players, even when the deal looks difficult.
 The bigger issue is making sure the shortlist is strong and realistic. If Porro ends up at Barcelona or Real Madrid, Liverpool cannot be left scrambling. There needs to be a clear plan, with two or three alternatives ready to go. Right-back has become too important in elite football to leave to chance.
 There is still hope that Bradley returns well and makes the role his own. That would be the best outcome of all. But if there is any doubt, Liverpool have to be ruthless, proactive and ambitious. This position could shape the balance of the whole side.
